## Keywords

## 2.1 One account, many services

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- You prove an account is yours with something you know, have or are.
- With single sign-on, one sign-in opens many services.
- On a lab computer, sign out and never save your password.
- **Lab task:** Sign in once. How many services open?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/sso.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Accounts and sign-in

a) A code comes to your phone. Is it something you know, have or are?
b) You sign in one time, and e-mail and e-learning both open. What is this called?
c) You leave your lab desk for one minute. What should you do?

::: {.answer}
a) something you have
b) single sign-on
c) lock the screen (Windows key + L)
:::

## 2.2 Folders and paths

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Folders inside folders make a tree.
- A path is the full address of a file, from the top folder down to the file.
- Two files can have the same name, but never the same path.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/folder-tree.png)
:::
::::

## Extensions and sizes

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- The extension shows the type of a file, like `.docx` or `.jpg`.
- Always show extensions: `invoice.pdf.exe` is a program.
- Each size unit is 1024 times the one before: KB, MB, GB.
- **Lab task:** Turn on file name extensions. What are the size and the extension of three files?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/file-types.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 2 · Paths, types and sizes

a) Two files are both called `cv.docx`. What is always different?
b) A file is called `photo.jpg.exe`. What is it really?
c) A video is 3 GB. How many MB is it?

::: {.answer}
a) their paths
b) a program
c) 3 × 1024 = 3072 MB
:::

## 2.3 Good file names: date, content, version

| Poor name | Better name |
|---|---|
| New Document (3).docx | 2026-10-21_cv_v01.docx |
| final final.pptx | 2026-11-12_english-talk_v03.pptx |
| IMG_4821.jpg | 2026-10-21_family-dinner.jpg |

## 2.4 Sync is not backup

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Sync keeps the same files everywhere, also your mistakes.
- A backup is an extra copy in a separate place.
- The 3-2-1 rule: 3 copies, 2 kinds of storage, 1 in another place.
- **Lab task:** Delete a test file, then get it back from the recycle bin.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/sync-backup.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3–4 · Names and backup

a) Which date format sorts files by date: 21-10-2026 or 2026-10-21?
b) You delete a file on one device, and it is gone on all of them. Why?
c) What is a copy of your work on a USB stick at home?

::: {.answer}
a) 2026-10-21 (year-month-day)
b) The files are synced.
c) a backup
:::

## Try it 5 · Sara's report (harder)

The facts: Sara's document `final final (2).docx` is from 5 November 2026. The folder is synced; a USB copy is at home.

a) What is a better name for the document?
b) She deletes the folder by mistake. Where can she get it back first?
c) What is her USB copy at home in the 3-2-1 rule?

::: {.answer}
a) 2026-11-05_report_v01.docx
b) the cloud recycle bin
c) the copy in another place
:::

## Summary

- You prove an account is yours with something you know, have or are.
- A path is the full address of a file in the folder tree.
- Show extensions; each size unit is 1024 times the one before.
- Good names have the date, what the file is, and a version.
- Sync copies your mistakes; a backup does not.
